<entry id="A02402">
<head-word>אַסְטְרֹולֹוגֹוס, </head-word>
<head-word>(אַצְ', </head-word>
<head-word>; , </head-word>
<head-word>אִיסְ', </head-word>
<head-word>אִיצְ')</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (ἀστρολόγος) 
<italic>astronomer; astrologer</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Sabb. VI, 8
<sup>d</sup> top חדא אי' (read חד) a certain astrol.; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. אַסְטְרֹולֹוגִין</plural-form> (אַצְ' &c.). Targ. I Chron. XII, 32 ed. Rahm. איצרולוגין (Var. איצטרו'). Ex. R. 1; a. v. fr.—Cant. R. to VII, 9 אַסְטְרֹולֹוגֹוסֵי. [Yalk. Ex. 164 איסטרוגילין, a. other corruptions, corr. acc.]—V. also next w.—[As regards צט for סט, v. Recens. Don. b. Librat ed. Filipp. p. 9.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02403">
<head-word>אַסְטְרֹולֹוגְיָא, </head-word>
<head-word>(אִיסְ', </head-word>
<head-word>אסת', </head-word>
<head-word>), , </head-word>
<head-word>(אִיצְ') אַצְ'</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (ἀστρολογία) 
<italic>astronomy</italic>, mostly 
<italic>astrology, sooth-saying, astrological prediction</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ab. Zar. II, 41
<sup>a</sup> top הוה חמי בא' דידיה he foresaw by dint of astrol. speculation (prob. to be read גין …, v. infra). Pesik. R. s. 14 אסטרוגילא (corr. acc.; cmp. טְיָיר).—
<plural-form>Pl. אַסְטְרֹולֹוגִין</plural-form> prop. 
<italic>astrologers</italic>, trnsf. 
<italic>astrological books, implements, horoscope</italic> &c. Gen. R. s. 85 רואה היתה בא' וכ' she saw in her astrological books (or horoscope). Deut. R. s. 8 מביט באסטרולוגים; Lev. R. s. 36 אצטרוגליס, לוגים … &c. (corr. acc.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02406">
<head-word>אִסְטְרֹונְגִּילֹון</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> adv. (στρογγύλον, or στρογγυλοῦν, S.) 
<italic>in a rounded way, circularly</italic> (opp. τετράγωνον, or τετραγώνιον).</definition>
<notes> Pesik. R. s. 10, read: שלא היו יושבין טטרגונין או שורה ארוכה אלא א' כחצי גורן עגולה וכ' they sat not forming a square or a long line, but in a semi-circle, like the shape of a half of the rounded court-room (v. גֹּורֶן), so that they could conveniently see each other. V. בוטרגנין.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02407">
<head-word>אִסְטְרֹופֹומָטָא, </head-word>
<head-word>אִיסְ'</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (variously corrupted, v. infra)
<pos> m. pl.</pos> (στροφώματα) 
<italic>pivots, pins at top and bottom of a door turning in sockets</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 66 כמין א' הדלתות וכ' Ar. (ed. איסטריפומיטא; Yalk. Gen. 115 איסטדומוטא) pivotlike, the doors could be doubled backward. [Yalk. l. c. may be read אסטרופוטא στρόφωμτος, v. LXX, Ezek. XLI, 24.] Midd. IV, 1 איצטרבאמוטא Ar., ed. איצטרמיטה (corr. as above). Pesik. B’shall. p. 86
<sup>b</sup>; Yalk. Sam. 152 כאילין אמפומטא &c. (corr. acc.) like doors turning in sockets.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02408">
<head-word>אִסְטְרָטָא, </head-word>
<head-word>אִיסְטְ', </head-word>
<head-word>אִסְטְרָטָה</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> c. </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> (interchanging with אִסְרָטָא, סְרָטָא, trnsp. אסטרא; 
<italic>strata</italic>, sub. via, στρᾶτα S.) 
<italic>paved way, public road</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. II Num. XX, 17 … טה; a. fr.—Y. Gitt. IV, beg. 45
<sup>c</sup>. Y. Snh. II, 20
<sup>a</sup> top גו א' וכ' on the road he heard &c. Tosef. Sabb. X (XI) 1 sq. (סרטא, אסרטא, Var. אסתרטא with ת). Ab. d’R. N. XXVIII life is like לאיסטרטיא וכ' (read … טא) a public road running between two paths &c. Koh. R. to VII, 7 הוינא עקים אִסְטְרָטִי I was bending my road, went out of my way.—
<plural-form>Pl. אִסְטְרָטַיָּא,</plural-form> (אִסְטַרְטַיָּא, incorr. אִסְטְרַטְיָא). Targ. Y. Num. XX, 19.—אִסְטְרָטִין usu. 
<italic>the city walks, promenades</italic> (between the colonnades &c.). Y. Sabb. VI, 8
<sup>a</sup> bot. הוו מטיילין בא' were promenading &c. Y. Kil. IX, 32
<sup>d</sup> top; Cant. R. to V, 13; Y. Keth. XII, 35
<sup>b</sup> bot. אסטרין. [Deut. R. s. 3 אסטרטין, read אסטרטיגין.] [In Targ. mostly אִסְרָטִין, אסטרין.]</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>theatre.</italic></definition>
<notes>
<plural-form>Pl. אִסְטְרָטָאֹות,</plural-form> v. אִסְטַרְיָא.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02412">
<head-word>אִסְטְרַטְיָא, </head-word>
<head-word>אִיסְ', </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (στρατεία, in the sense of στρατόπεδον) 
<italic>camp, encampment</italic>, esp. 
<italic>an open space in</italic>
<pgbrk id="pg92" />
<italic>front of the royal palace, court;</italic> also 
<italic>station on the road</italic> for Temple pilgrims.</definition>
<notes> Erub. 26
<sup>a</sup> א' של מלכים Ms. M. (ed. מלך) camp or court round the royal palace. [Men. 103
<sup>b</sup> איסטריא של מלך, for איסטרטיא(?), v. however אִסְטַרְיָא.] [Lam. R. to III, 7 באידנא א'; Ab. d’R. Nath. XXVIlI לאי', read אִסְטְרָטָא. Targ. Y. Num. XX, 19 רַטְיָא … some ed., v. אִסְטְרָטָא.]—
<plural-form>Pl. אִסְטְרַטְיָאֹות</plural-form>. M. Kat. 5
<sup>a</sup> Ms. M. (ed. טאות …); Mekh. B’shall. Vayissa ch. III א' 
<italic>stations</italic> (= רחובות). [Erub. l. c. טיא … שהיו …, read שהיא, or … יאות; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02413">
<head-word>אִסְטְרַטְיָא, </head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<head-word>(אִסְרַטְיָא), </head-word>
<head-word>אִיסְ'</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (στρατία) prop. 
<italic>army;</italic> hence </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>host</italic> (of heavens, cmp. LXX Neh. IX, 6).</definition>
<notes> Num. R. s. 12 א' של מעלה; Midr. Till. to Ps. XCII, end אסר' … divine army (angels, prophets &c.)</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>royal suite, court-officers</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kidd. IV, 5 מוכתב בא' של מלך recorded in the king’s list of officers (during Agrippa’s reign, serving as evidence of legitimate birth; cmp. אַרְכִי I). Lam. R. to II, 2 אסט'; Y. Taan. IV, 68
<sup>d</sup> bot. אסר' the list of Barkokhba’s suite. [Y. Ned. XI, 42
<sup>d</sup> bot. אסטרטיות read אִסְטְרַטְיֹוטֹות; ib. אסטרטיות חבק' read אִסְטְרַטְיוֹט. Y. Gitt. III, 45
<sup>a</sup> top. אסטרטיות, v. אַפָּרָטֹוסֹות. Tanḥ. B’resh. 2 אסטרטיאות, Var. אסטראות, v. אִסְטַרְיָא.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02414">
<head-word>אִסְטַרְטֵיג, </head-word>
<head-word>אִסְטַרְטֵיגָא</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (στρατήγιον) 
<italic>camp, regular garrison</italic> (= h. מַצַּב), contrad. to stragglers &c. Targ. I Sam. XIII, 23; XIV, 1; 4; 6; 16; a. e.—
<plural-form>Pl. אִסְטַרְטִיגִין</plural-form>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. II Sam. VIII, 6 (h. text נציבים). Targ. I Sam. X, 5 … אִסְטַרְטִיגֵי (constr.).—גַיָּא … Targ. I Kings IV, 5 על א' chief of camps.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02415">
<head-word>(אסטרטיג) אִסְטַרְטֵיגֹוס</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (στρατηγός) 
<italic>military commander, general</italic>; (in later Greek) 
<italic>prefect, city-magistrate</italic>; also 
<italic>chief of body guards</italic> (στρατηγὸς τῶν πραισενταλίων, D.</definition>
<notes> C.). Ex. R. s. 31 (cmp. Gen. R. s. 58). Ib. s. 37, beg.; a. fr.—Deut. R. s. 10 לאסטרטיגין וכ' (read … גֹוס); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. אִסְטַרְטֵיגִין, אִסְטַרְטֵיגֵי</plural-form>.—Targ. II, Esth. I, 3 איסתרת' (corr. acc.) 
<italic>generals</italic>. Y. Ber. VIII, 12
<sup>c</sup> top שני א' two chiefs of guards; Gen. R. s. 3; a. fr.—B. Bath. 143
<sup>a</sup> בולי ואסטרטיגי Ms. M. (ed. אבולי ואסטרוגי); Y. Yoma I, 39
<sup>a</sup> top כולי ואסרטיגי (read בולי ואסטרטיגי, v. בּוּלִי II). Yalk. Koh. 969 אמר לאסטרון שלו (read לאסטרטיגין) he ordered his guard.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02416">
<head-word>אִסְטְרַטְיֹוט, </head-word>
<head-word>אִסְטְרַטְיֹוטָא, </head-word>
<head-word>אִסְטְרַטְיֹוטֵיס</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (στρατιώτης) prop. 
<italic>soldier</italic>, later 
<italic>Roman officer</italic> (D. C. Gr. s. v.); 
<italic>attendant</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Shek. V, 49
<sup>a</sup>; Cant. R. to III, 6, end אסטרטיג (corr. acc.). Y. Keth. I, 25
<sup>c</sup> top טיוס … (corr. acc.).—
<plural-form>Pl. אִסְטְרַטְיֹוטִין</plural-form>. Targ. I Chr. XVIII, 6 (v. however Targ. II Sam. VIII, 6). Tanḥ. Haăz. 2, read: באו א' the officers came to meet the king.—אִסְטְרַטְיֹוטֹות. Y. B. Kam. IV, 4
<sup>b</sup> top ששליח המלכות שני א' (read ששלחה) the Roman governm. sent two commissioners. Y. Ned. XI, 42
<sup>d</sup> bot. אסטרטיות; v. אִסְטְרַטְיָא II.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02422">
<head-word>אִסְטַרְיָא, </head-word>
<head-word>אִסטַרְיָה, </head-word>
<head-word>אִסְטַרְיָיא, </head-word>
<head-word>אִיסְ', </head-word>
<head-word>אִצְ', </head-word>
<head-word>אִיצְ'</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> f. 
<alternative>(also אִסְטָרָא m.)</alternative> cacophemistic appellations of all kinds of gentile sports; cmp. the use of θέατρον and θεατρίζειν in Ad Corinth.</definition>
<notes> I, IV, 9, a. Hebr. X, 33; אסטריא &c., as if a denomin. of סרר, cmp. Syr. אסטרניא, אצטרניא, P. Sm. 304 a. cit. ibid.; אצטריבא, as if fr. צרב; אצטרדיון (v. next w.) as if fr. צרד, v. אִיצְטַדִּין; cmp. אֲבֵידָן) 
<italic>theatre, arena, gladiatorial shows</italic>, &c. Ab. Zar. I, 7 (16
<sup>a</sup>) גרדום אצטדייא וכ' (Ms. M. אצטריבא, but in Gem. 18
<sup>b</sup> repeatedly אצטריא; Y. ed. איסטדייא; Mish. Nap. אצטדיא, comment. אצטרדיא) place of execution, of shows &c.; v. Gem. 18
<sup>b</sup>.—[Men. 103
<sup>b</sup> איסטריא של מלך the king’s amphitheatre, v. אסטרטיא]. 
<plural-form>Pl. אִסְטַרְיוֹת</plural-form>. Sifra Aḥaré Par. IX ch. 13. Tanḥ. B’resh. 2 אִסְטְרָאוֹת Var. (ed. אִסְטְרָטָאוֹת). Ab. Zar. 18
<sup>b</sup> אשר לא הלך לאיסטרטאות Ms. M. (ed. לטרטיאות, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.).—אִסְטָרִין, v. next w.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A02423">
<head-word>אִסְטָרִין, </head-word>
<head-word>אִצְטָרִין, </head-word>
<head-word>אִיסְ', </head-word>
<head-word>אִיצְ'</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (אִצְטַרְטְיוֹן, אִצְטַרְרְּיוֹן, אִיצְטַרְיוֹן, also with rejection of א' after prefixes)
<pos> m.</pos> (pl. of אסטרא, v. 
<xref rid="A02422">preced.</xref>; used as sing.</definition>
<notes>, sub. בית ה־ &c.) 
<italic>arena, theatre</italic>. B. Kam. IV, 4 (39
<sup>a</sup>) שור האיצטרין Ms. M. (ed. איצטדין, Ms. H. a. R., a. Mish. Nap., a. Y. ed. איסטדין) an ox of the arena (that killed a person). Tosef. Ab. Zar. II, 7 היושב באסטרין וכ' Var. (ed. Zuck. איסטרטון, ed. איסטרין) he who visits the amphitheatre is considered a murderer (countenancing bloodshed); Y. ib. I, 40
<sup>a</sup> איצטדון (interchanging with תיאטרין).—

<number>—3)</number>

<italic>Asmakhta</italic> (
<italic>surety</italic>), 
<italic>a promise to submit to a forfeiture of pledged property</italic> (
<italic>or equivalent</italic>) 
<italic>without having received a sufficient consideration; collateral security with the condition of forfeiture beyond the amount to be secured;</italic> e.g. A pays a portion of his indebtedness to B, leaving the bill of debt as a security in the hands of a third party, and agreeing to pay 
<italic>the full amount</italic> on the bill, if, at a stipulated time, he should fail to pay the due balance.</definition>
<notes> B. Bath. 168
<sup>a</sup> א' לא קניא 
<italic>asmakhta</italic> does not purchase, gives no title, i.e. gives the claimant no rights (because the law presumes that he who made such a promise, could not have meant it seriously but had in view only to give his transaction the character of good faith and solemnity); ibid. א' קניא 
<italic>asm.</italic> is a valid legal transfer of property. B. Mets. 66
<sup>a</sup>; 73
<sup>b</sup>. Ned. 27
<sup>b</sup>; a. e.—Snh. 24
<sup>b</sup> applied to
